extraction_scope.mechanism_boundaries: No direct bacterial membrane permeabilization assay was recovered; membrane-disruption language remains design/background inference. Cellular anti-inflammatory pathway evidence is source-supported for selected peptides.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: WALK peptides were designed as short cationic amphipathic helical peptides, and CD data support increased helical structure in TFE/SDS membrane-mimetic environments.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: WALK244 and WALK243 peptide series; examples WALK244.04 and WALK243.04
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports conformation in membrane-mimetic solvents and does not by itself prove a direct antibacterial killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper frames antibacterial action as anticipated from amphipathic helical properties and bacterial biomembrane interaction, but it does not report a direct membrane permeabilization assay for the WALK244/WALK243 antibacterial activity.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Keep membrane-disruption language as inferred/background mechanism context, not direct_mechanism evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Selected peptides, especially WALK244.04 and WALK243.04, reduce LPS-stimulated inflammatory readouts in macrophage assays, including NO release and downstream inflammatory signaling/protein-expression readouts.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: WALK244.04 and WALK243.04 in J774A.1 and RAW264.7 macrophage contexts
mechanism_claims.limitations: The exact bar values are figure-only and are not promoted to tabular activity rows; the supported claim is direction/assay class and selected-peptide anti-inflammatory phenotype.
